segments.title: A first look at Mikasa in Yokosuka
segments.summary: After reaching Mikasa just before 9:00 and finding the site already closed, this first exterior view sets up a return when the museum opens the next morning.
segments.body: The visit reaches Mikasa just after the site has closed, so this first encounter is limited to the ship's exterior. Her appearance is enough to build anticipation for a return when the museum is scheduled to open at 8:00 the next morning. The short walk around the site introduces Mikasa as a preserved warship in Yokosuka before any detailed interpretation begins. It is a visual first look rather than an account of the ship's history.

evidence.note: He arrives shortly before closing, identifies Mikasa, and plans to return when the site opens.

segments.title: Mikasa beside the modern naval presence at Yokosuka
segments.summary: Mikasa's surviving hull and 12-inch guns are set against the nearby United States Navy presence in Yokosuka.
segments.body: Mikasa is described as the last remaining ship of her type, standing in a Yokosuka setting where the U.S. Navy is immediately next door. Her 12-inch guns prompt a joke about whether the old battleship is watching the modern naval presence or being watched by it. The contrast places a preserved warship beside an active naval base. This moment offers a visual comparison between an older form of sea power and the port that surrounds it.

evidence.note: He describes Mikasa as the last remaining ship of her type and notes her 12-inch guns beside the nearby US Navy.
